The Related Aircraft and Equipment tab displays a list of the end-item Assets that the current Model is applied to.
The "Current Configuration" tab is used to understand details on the current configuration status of a configuration-managed asset.
ACM provides dedicated Object Structures which can be used to load relevant data loaded through the Maximo Integration Framework (MIF).

The "Maintenance Plan" tab is used to understand the open "Maintenance Events" which exists for a configuration managed asset. Maintenance Events are persisted in the table "PLUSALFEVENT" The system maintains a single maintenance event for each open corrective (non PM generated) work order that exists for an Asset. Once the work order associated with a Maintenance Event is completed then the event is placed into history. These historical maintenance events are then visible on the Maintenance History tab. In addition, one or more maintenance events are created and managed for each active PM that exists for the selected asset. In the case of active PMs, one maintenance event is managed for each frequency criteria defined on the PM. In addition multiple additional maintenance events may exist for a single PM if there are multiple open work orders for the PM. For example an active PM, with both a calendar and meter based frequency, would display two rows for the PM on the Maintenace Plan tab. Each maintenance event gives information relating to the frequency information and when it is next due, including time or meter units remaining. It may also contain a link to the Work Order (if an open work order exists for the PM) Due to the way the Maintenance Event records are managed by the system, it enables a user to easily view and understand the open scheduled and corrective work that exists for configuration-managed assets. In addition, a full history of all work performed can be easily viewed and understood. The Maintenance Plan also enables the user to view the active maintenance for the selected asset at any "As of Date", either at the current date and time or at a point in time in the past. Note that if a PMs status is changed to INACTIVE then the system will either: Delete the maintenance events(s) if there are no open work orders for the PM. 2) Retain the maintenance event(s) for each open PM work order for the inactive PM. These maintenance event(s) are retained until such time that the work order is completed (at which point they are place into history). If the work order is cancelled then the maintenance event is deleted.

Maintenance Event records are utilised by the BDI to determine whether specific problem codes should be reported. These are described below: Problem Code Description Explanation EBA Event beyond alert The active PM is past either its Alert Date or Alert Count. EBW Event beyond warning The active PM is past either its Warning Date or Warning Count. EBD Event beyond due The active PM is past either its Due Date or Date Count ENR Event needs review The active PM requires manual review to ensure its Due Date / Count are accurate.

documents.t: Frequency: The frequency value defining the interval at which a PM should be completed. This can be either calendar or meter based. Meter Unit: The meter unit description or calendar unit for the frequency interval. Active: Either the date and time at which the maintenance event became active or the meter count for the asset when maintenance event was activated. In the case of a PM record for a calendar based frequency, this is typically the date and time the PM was last last performed. For a PM record with a meter based frequency this is the meter count when the the PM was last performed. For a corrective maintenance work order this displays the Reported Date of the work order. Since: This field displays either the number of days or meter units recorded since the maintenance event became active. For a calendar PM or correct maintenance event this is the number of days since the PM was last performed or number of days since the work order was raised. For a meter based PM the field displays the number of meter units accumulated since the PM was last performed. Due: This field displays either the Due Date (for calendar PMs or deferred work orders) or the meter count at which the work is due (for meter PMs or work orders deferred by a meter value). End Item Due Count: The count at which the work is due at the end item level (top level asset). Deferrals: Checkbox which, if true, indicates that a work order has been deferred. Deferrals are perfomed in the Work Order Tracking (CM) application. Left: The number of days or meter units remaining before the work is due. Work Order: A work order number. Explanation of field values in the table detail: Active Date Reviewed: This checkbox indicates if the frequency information for the maintenance event needs to be reviewed. This checbox is generally set to false for PMs that were created automatically by the system. For example, if a new Master PM was made active and the system created PMs for the assets with the same CM Items as listed on the Master PM. In this scenario, it requires that a user must manually review the maintenance event and ensure that the point at which is next due is acccurate. If it is then the checkbox can be set to true and the record saved. If the checkbox is set to false the BDI will raise a ENR (Event Needs Review) problem code for the PM. This is considered to be an INVALID configuration as scheduled maintenance is active but not correctly initialised. The system will not automatically created work orders for PMs where the associated maintenance event is marked as needing review. Current Count: For meter based maintenance events, displays the current total for the meter. Last Date: Displays the last date that the PM was completed. Last Count: Displays the meter count at the date of last PM completion (relevant for meter based events only). Active Date: The date and time at which the maintenance event became active. Normally this would be the same as the date the PM was last completed. For corrective maintenance this is the report date of the work order. A further explanation of how this effects alert, warning and due date/count calculations is decribed in detail later in this topic. Alert Date: The Alert Date of the maintenance event. Applicable for calendar based PMs only. The BDI will generate a work order automatically when the alert date is reached or exceeded. An EBA (Event Beyond Alert) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Alert Date. Warning Date: The Warning Date of the maintenance event. Applicable for calendar based PMs only. An EBW (Event Beyong Warning) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Warning Date. Due Date: The Due Date of the maintenance event. Applicable for calendar based PMs only. An EBD (Event Beyond Due) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Due Date. Active Count: The meter total for the asset at the Active Date. See later in the topic for an explanation of the logic around meter calculations in relation to maintenance events. Alert Count: The Alert Count of the maintenance event. Applicable for meter based PMs only. The BDI will generate a work order automatically when the alert dcountate is reached or exceeded. An EBA (Event Beyond Alert) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Alert Count. Warning Count: The Warning Count of the maintenance event. Applicable for meter based PMs only. An EBW (Event Beyong Warning) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Warning Count. Due Count: The Due Count of the maintenance event. Applicable for meter based PMs only. An EBD (Event Beyond Due) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Due Count.

documents.t: Both the "Due Date" and/or "Due Count" for a Maintenance Event record is calculated based on the Active Date recorded on the maintenance event and the Frequency/Interval of the associated PM. These calculations are described below Calendar Frequencies: Due Date = (Active Date + Calendar Frequency) - Due Count Offset Note: The "Due Count Offset" is optional but can be used to adjust the Due Date in the case where the Active Date + Calendar Frequency does not give the desired due date value. When PM "Alert and Warning Interval State" = Absolute from Active: Alert Date = (Active Date + Alert Interval) - Due Count Offset Warning Date = (Active Date + Warning Interval) - Due Count Offset When PM "Alert and Warning Interval State" = Absolute Prior to Due: Alert Date = Due Date - Alert Interval Warning Date = Due Date - Warning Interval Meter Frequencies: The calculation for meter based maintenance events involves the use of the calculated life algorithm. Due Count = (Active Count) + Meter Frequency) - Due Count Offset Where Active Count = The meter total derived by the calculated life algorithm for the asset at the Active Date. Note: The "Due Count Offset" can be used to adjust the Due Count in the case where the Active Count + Meter Frequency does not give the desired due count value. When PM "Alert and Warning Interval State" = Absolute from Active: Alert Count = (Active Count + Alert Interval) - Due Count Offset Warning Count = (Active Count + Warning Interval) - Due Count Offset When PM "Alert and Warning Interval State" = Absolute Prior to Due: Alert Count = Due Count - Alert Interval Warning Count = Due Count - Warning Interval

documents.t: The Modification Status tab displays information and the status of Technical Records which are applicable to the current configuration-managed asset. A number of options are provided to filter the table(s) displayed on the tab. When an option checkbox is changed the "Refresh View" button should be clicked to update the data within the tables: Option Description Include Children? When set to true, this checkbox causes a second Modification Status table to be displayed. The table list the modification status of Technical Records against the sub assembly assets within the main asset hierarchy. Fully Embodied? When set to true, the tables will display any Technical Records which have been fully embodied (complied with) for the asset(s) Active? When set to true, the tables will display any Technical Records are active and applicable to the asset(s) but have not yet been complied with. Partially Embodied? When set to true, the tables will display any Technical Records which are active but have only been partially emboded. This is a special status to indicate work may have been started against the asset but has not yet been fully embodied (eg a two part service bulletin). Not Applicable? When set to true, the table will display any Technical Records which are active against the asset but have been marked as not applicable. Each table provides details on the specific Technical Records which are active and applicable to the asset. It includes details of when and by whom the change was performed by.

This page gives an overview and explanation of the capability and logic used in Maximo Aviation to manage asset install and removal transactions. The install/remove functionality, provided for configuration-managed assets, is designed in such a way as to record a complete history of the installation and removal history of configuration-managed assets. It is also designed in such a way as to provide the ability to perform retrospective or out of sequence transactions. The aim of this documentation is to provide users of Maximo Aviation with guidance as to this logic, how the data is persisted and how it is presented to the user within the ACM interface. The installation and removal history of configuration-managed assets is persisted in the table: PLUSASAONOFF Each individual PLUSASAONOFF record records either: A period of time where an asset was installed into a parent assembly. A period of time where an asset was NOT installed into a parent assembly. A period of time where a specific position within an asset assembly structure was empty. Due to the way this information is persisted within this table, the system provides the ability to view the sub assembly structure at any point in time (Referred to as the "As of Date") in the assets lifecycle.

A list of the main attributes of the PLUSASAONOFF table is detailed below: Attribute Name Data Type Description ASSETID BIGINT The installed Asset identifier. For PLUSASASONOFF records representing periods where a position in a parent assembly was empty this value is NULL. PARENTASSETID BIGINT The Parent Asset identifier. For PLUSASASONOFF records representing periods where an Asset was not installed this value is NULL. ONTIME DATETIME The date and time at which either: 1. An asset was installed into a parent assembly. 2. The beginning of the period of time where an asset was NOT installed into a parent assembly. 3 The beginning of the period of time for which a position within a parent assembly was empty. The PLUSASAONOFF.ONTIME should be populated on all PLUSASAONOFF records. OFFTIME DATETIME The date and time at which either 1. An asset was removed from a parent assembly. 2. The end of the period of time where an asset was NOT installed into a parent assembly. 3 The end of the period of time for which a position within a parent assembly was empty. The PLUSASONOFF.OFFTIME maybe NULL and this represents the "current" data about the asset or position. LABEL UPPER The Label of the position POSITION UPPER The Position code of the position NAME UPPER The Build Item name of the position LCN UPPER The LCN of the position CURTOPASSET BIGINT The asset identifier of the asset at the top of the current assembly. NONTRACKED YORN =1 if the position is flagged as non-tracked in the Models Build Hierarchy. NONSERIALIZED YORN =1 if the position is flagged as non-serialized in the Models Build Hierarchy. SOFTWARE YORN =1 if the position is flagged as a software position in the Models Build Hierarchy. TYPE UPPER The Type of the transaction (described in detail below)

In order for the system to provide the ability to record installation and removal transactions out of chronological sequence a "Type" value is recorded on each PLUSASAONOFF record. This is used to signify additional information about the transaction for the purposes of transaction integrity. Four possible "Type" values exist: Type Value Description G (Gap) A PLUSASAONOFF record with a Type=G, represents either: 1. A period of time between 2 dates when a position is empty (PLUSASAONOFF.ASSETID IS NULL) or; 2. A period of time where a sub assembly asset is not installed (PLUSASAONOFF.PARENTASSETID IS NULL). If the Off Time is null on the record with Type=G this reflects that the position is currently empty or the asset is not currently installed. N (Valid On) Signifies that the date on which the asset was installed (PLUSASAONOFF.ONTIME) into a parent assembly is a confirmed date. I.e. An explicit installation transaction was carried out to install the asset into a parent assembly. If the the Type of the Transaction=N but the Off Date is populated then this "Off Date" value was assumed by the system. This assumption is based on the fact that no explicit removal transaction was recorded. This is considered by the system to be invalid configuration history (explained further below). F (Value Off) Signifies that a confirmed removal of an asset from a parent assembly took place at the Off Date but there was no corresponding confirmed installation of this asset into the parent assembly and position. In this situation the On Date and Time had to be assumed by the system (explained further below). B (Both N and F are valid) Signifies that Both the On Date and Off Dates and times were confirmed transactions. Invalid Configuration History Situations​ If the installation and removal of assets are recorded within the system in the same chronological order and with the same transaction dates as those with they were performed physically then the PLUSASAONOFF records would not normally require modification. However, in circumstances where a mistake is made or the chronology is wrongly reported or incomplete then the BDI may report a Problem Code of ISR (Invalid Installation and Removal History). This can happen under the following two conditions: TYPE = N AND OFFTIME IS NOT NULL: This indicates an "assumed" removal needed to be performed. In this situation, where an install of the asset is performed into one position without explicitly performing a removal of the asset from another (different) position. One scenario where this can occur is when a user installs an asset, which is already installed into another parent and position at the "As of Date", but the user fails to first remove the asset from its existing parent/position. To correct this a removal transaction must be performed for the asset with a transaction date that is after the "On Date" but on or before the assumed removal date. If the assumed removal date is correct then the user can confirm this by modifying the Off Date in the Position History tab and setting it back to the date and time of the removal then saving. TYPE = F: This indicates an Asset was removed from a parent assembly but there was no confirmed prior installation of the asset into the position within that parent assembly. One scenario where this may occur is when an asset is removed at one "As of Date" and then another removal is performed at an earlier "As of Date" (from the same parent and position). To correct this an installation transaction must be performed for the asset, into the relevant position, with a transaction data between the dates of the two removal (F) transactions.

The Assets (CM) application allows a user to understand the status of configuration-managed Assets. Assets (CM) is a clone of the standard Maximo Assets application. It contains additional fields, tabs and actions so that the user can understand the status of configuration managed assets. It also provides additional actions so a user can update the as-maintained configuration data of CM managed assets.

The list page displays a list of Assets included CM managed and non-CM managed Assets. To display only CM managed assets the user can filter on the "CM Item" field with the "not null" filter value: "!=null" BDI Status Icons​ The page also displays an icon indicating the Configuration (BDI) Status for CM Managed Assets. The possible icon values are: Icon Status Description OK Configuration status is OK and no problems currently exist. INVALID A critical problem exists for the assets configuration that should be investigated and remedied. ALERT The asset has a configuration status that a user should be aware of but immediate action may not be necessary. UNKNOWNN The configuraiton status of the asset is unknown. This is used when no configuration status records exist for the asset Normally this is because the asset has not yet been validated by the BDI.
The main "Asset" page of the Assets (CM) application contains a number of addtional fields containing the CM related attributes of the Asset.

The "View" tab is used to understand the as maintained configuration data for a configuration managed asset. It is hidden (using Maximo conditional UI) for assets which are not configuration managed. The top section of the screen contains the following fields, buttons and UI components: Asset Hierarchy​ The Asset Hierarchy UI component provides a hierarchical view of a configuration managed asset assembly. It displays key information, taken from the corresponding build postions within the related Model, such as Label, Position, Position Name and LCN. In addition each node in the hiearchy displays information about the Asset installed into the position: Asset Number, Serial Number and CM Item. Clicking on the BDI Status icon at the far right of each node in the hierarchy opens the BDI Status dialog for the asset in the position. As of Date​ The "As of Date" field defaults to the current system date and time when the user enters the application. The user can change this date to a point in time in the past to understand what the configuration status of the Asset was at this point in time. When a user changes the "As of Date" field value, and tabs out of the field, the Asset Hierarchy will be updated to display the Asset Hierarchy as it was at this date and time. Now Button​ Clicking the "Now" button updates the "As of Date" field to the current system date and time. It then automatically refreshes the Asset Hierarchy view so that it displays the current as maintained configuration of the asset assembly. Perspective​ The Perspective field contains a list of Systems which have been defined in the associated Model. The default Perspective is the physical Asset Hierarchy corresponding to the main Build Hierarchy in the Model. Systems can be used to define functional system views within the Model to aid users in understanding which assets form part of particular functional systems within the Asset assembly.

Right clicking a node in the Asset Hierarchy opens a context menu with a list of actions that can be performed against the selected position. The actions provided by each item in the menu are listed below. Each action opens a dedicated dialog for the specific action: Action Description Install/Remove Asset Provides the ability to install / removal of a child asset from the selected position. It is used from installing removing assets from Sub Assembly positions or Installation Point positions. Switch Equipment Positions Provides the ability to "switch" multiple assets between positions within the current asset assembly. The positions must be created from the same Build Item in the Model to allow the switch to take place. Install/Remove Assets From Serialized Build Position Provides the ability to installed/remove assets ina multiple serialized quantity position. Non-Serialized Build Position Provides the ability to update the quantity of CM Items associated with a non-serialized build position. Change CM Item Provides the ability to change the CM Item associated with a CM Managed asset. Change Registration Provides the ability to change the Registration of a CM Managed asset. This action can only be performed against end item assets. Change Serial Provides the ability to change the Serial number of a CM Managed asset. CM Item Change History Displays the history of changes to the CM Item of a CM Managed Asset. Registration Change History Displays the history of changes to the Registration of a CM Managed End-Item Asset. Serial Change History Displays the history of changes to the Serial Number of a CM Managed Asset. View Configuration Change History Displays the history of changes to the Configuration of a CM Managed Asset End-Item Asset CM Rules Displays the CM Rule information for the selected position. BDI Status Opens the BDI Status dialog for the selected position.

A series of sub tabs is displayed at bottom of the Assets (CM) View tab. The information displayed in each tab relates to the node in the Asset Hierarchy that is currently selected. In addition the information displayed in the tab also reflects the current "As of Date" value.

The "Initial" tab displays the CONTINUOUS type meters (ASSETMETER records) associated with the CM Asset. Note that GAUGE and CHARACTERISTIC type meters are managed on the main "Meters" tab. Each Meter has to have an Initial Reading Date and Initial Count. These are used to initialise the point from which we wish to track the life of the asset within the Maximo system. All meter readings entered against the asset must have a Meter Reading Date later than the Initial Reading Date. The Initial Count should reflect the life of the meter at the Intial Reading Date. The Meter which is marked as the "Default" is used to calculate "TS Install" (Time Since Install) values displayed on the Parent, Child and Position History tabs. Explanation of Fields: "Current" : Displays the total for the Meter at the "As of Date". "Since" : Displays the number of meter units accumulated since the Initial Count (Since = Current - Initial Count). "Estimated?" : Indicates if the Intial Count for the Meter was estimated.

The "Direct" tab displays the CONTINUOUS type Meter Readings (METERREADING) that have been created directly against the asset selected in the Asset Hierarchy. Meter readings can be added, deleted or updated on this tab. Note that the meter reading date cannot be modified once a record is saved (only the meter value, either delta or actual depending on reading type). If a mistake is made with the reading date then the meter reading should be deleted and a new reading added with the correct date.

The "Summary" tab displays up to three rows for each continuous type meter for the selected asset. The "Type" for each row indicates what the count signifies: Initial Reading: The intial reading (taken from the ASSETMETER.PLUSANCHORCOUNT) for the asset. Direct: The total of the meter reading records created for the select asset. Indirect: The total number of meter units calculated for the asset based on readings against a higher assembly (during a period where the asset was installed into the higher assembly).

The "Maintenance Plan" tab displays any active Preventive Maintenance records for the selected asset. In addition it displays any open Work Orders (including both PM and corrective maintenance work orders). Together these records are termed "Maintenance Events". Due to the importance of the information contained within this tab the next topic is dedicated solely to this.

The BDI Queue Status application gives visibility on the BDI Queue and a history of the processing of Aicraft and Equipment (Assets) by the BDI. The application provides a list of all BDI Queue records, together with a status, how long they took to process and if there was an error. BDI Queue records are persisted in the database table: PLUSAANTRAN BDI Queue Status List Page

Information about errors are displayed in the the "stack trace" field which is displayed conditionally only when the status of the record is ERROR. This can be useful in helping to expedite the resolution of BDI errors when provided to a system administrator or as part of an IBM support case.

Status Description PENDING The BDI queue record is awaiting processing. INPROGRESS The validation of the Asset by the BDI is inprogress. QUEUEUD The asset is currently being processed by the BDI but a configuration change has resulted in the need to process it again. COMPLETE Validation of the Asset by the BDI is complete. ERROR An error occurred during the validation of the asset. Consult a system administrator to report details of the error. If BDI queue records remain in a PENDING state for an unreasonable amount of time this could indicate a bottleneck in the queue processing component of the BDI application. The number of queue workers (threads) maybe increased or a dedicated BDI instance responsible for processing queue records can be created. The BDI Configuration topic gives more details on these options.

The BDI Queue Status Application contains an action "Manage BDI End Points" which opens a dialog containing the settings used to determine the service used for BDI API calls. A record is created in this table by default, on Maximo Aviation installation, assuming there are no existing records in the table. If more than one BDI instance has been configured the dialog can be used to add these additional instances such that they will be candidates for BDI API requests. This can be useful if the number of simultaneous BDI requests, made from the BDI Status dialog by Maximo users, becomes too large for a single BDI instance to handle. A Maximo Item Set, Organization or Site can be associated with each End Point definition to cause requests for Assets, which match those values, to be routed to that instance. This can be useful for load balancing API requests. The port should always be configured as 9443 and the SSL toggle box set to "ON". The service host takes the form of: { instanceId }-{ workspaceId }-{ bdi-instance-name }.mas-{ instanceId }-manage.svc

In certain scenarios, BDI queue records may become stuck in an INPROGRESS state and fail to update to ERROR status when validation issues occur. This can happen when database connectivity issues or other system problems prevent the BDI from properly updating the PLUSAANTRAN record status after encountering an error during asset validation. Problem Scenario: The BDI encounters an error during asset validation Under normal circumstances, the BDI should update the PLUSAANTRAN record STATUS to ERROR If a database connectivity issue (e.g., DB2 connection problem) occurs, the status update may fail The record remains stuck in INPROGRESS state indefinitely There is no built-in BDI monitoring to detect and correct this situation once the database issue is resolved If the BDI pod is restarted, it will automatically delete any PLUSAANTRAN records with STATUS=INPROGRESS. However, this is not a recommended solution as it requires manual intervention. Recommended Solution: Maximo Escalation The recommended approach to handle stuck BDI queue records is to configure a Maximo Escalation that automatically detects and corrects records that have been in INPROGRESS state for an excessive period of time. Escalation Configuration Benefits​ A properly configured escalation provides: Automated Monitoring - Continuously checks for stuck queue records Configurable Frequency - Define how often the escalation runs (e.g., every 30 minutes) Configurable Threshold - Set the time period before a record is considered failed (e.g., 1 hour) Automatic Remediation - Updates stuck records to ERROR status with appropriate timestamps Notification Capability - Sends alerts to specific roles or recipients when issues are detected Audit Trail - Maintains complete processing history for troubleshooting Example Escalation Configuration​ The following example demonstrates a typical escalation configuration for managing stuck BDI queue records: Escalation Settings: Runs every: 30 minutes Monitors: PLUSAANTRAN records with STATUS=INPROGRESS Threshold: Records in INPROGRESS for over 1 hour Action: Set STATUS to ERROR and ENDDATE to current system date and time Notification: Alert designated roles/recipients Escalation Point Configuration​ The escalation point defines the conditions that trigger the escalation: Key Escalation Details: Applies To: PLUSAANTRAN (BDI Queue Status table) Condition: status=(select value from synonymdomain where domainid = 'PLUSAANTRANSTATUS' and maxvalue='INPROGRESS') Schedule: 30m (minutes) Active: Enabled Escalation Points Elapsed Time Attribute: STARTDATE Elapsed Time Interval: 1 Elapsed Time Unit: Hours Escalation Action Configuration​ The escalation action defines what happens when the conditions are met: Action Details: Action: PLUSAANTRAN_ERROR Description: Updates the PLUSAANTRAN status to ERROR Object: PLUSAANTRAN Type: Set Value Value : 'ERROR' Accessible From: Escalation Action Details: Action: PLUSAANTRAN_ENDDATE Object: PLUSAANTRAN Type: Set Value Value : :&DATETIME& Accessible From: Escalation Implementation Steps​ Navigate to Escalations Application Open the Escalations application in Maximo Create a new escalation record Configure Escalation Point Set "Applies To" to PLUSAANTRAN Define the condition to identify stuck records Set the schedule interval (e.g., 30 minutes) Configure Escalation Action Add action to set STATUS to ERROR Add action to set ENDDATE to current timestamp Optionally configure notifications Save the escalation action Activate the Escalation Test the Escalation Create a test scenario with a stuck INPROGRESS record Wait for the escalation to run Verify the record is updated correctly Confirm notifications are sent (if configured) Monitor and Adjust Adjust threshold timing if needed Refine notification recipients Best Practices​ Threshold Timing: Set the threshold based on typical BDI processing times Consider the complexity of your aircraft configurations Allow sufficient time for legitimate long-running validations Start with a conservative threshold (e.g., 1-2 hours) and adjust based on experience Escalation Frequency: Run frequently enough to catch issues promptly (e.g., every 30 minutes) Balance between responsiveness and system load Avoid running too frequently to prevent unnecessary database queries Notification Strategy: Notify system administrators and BDI support team Include relevant details in notification (Asset ID, Start Time, Duration) Use notification groups rather than individual email addresses Consider escalating to IBM support if issues persist Monitoring and Maintenance: Regularly review escalation execution logs Track the frequency of stuck records to identify systemic issues Investigate root causes when escalations trigger frequently Update escalation configuration as system behavior changes A properly configured escalation ensures that stuck BDI queue records are automatically detected and corrected, maintaining system reliability and providing visibility into processing issues without requiring manual intervention. Troubleshooting​ If the escalation is not working as expected: Verify the escalation is active and enabled Check the escalation schedule is configured correctly Confirm the condition logic correctly identifies stuck records Review Maximo logs for escalation execution errors Ensure the escalation has appropriate permissions to update PLUSAANTRAN records Test the condition query manually in the database to verify it returns expected records

documents.t: The Flight Log Book Setup application in Maximo Aviation defines the configuration templates for Flight Log Books used for one or more aircraft. Th application establishes the operational parameters, meter configurations, fuel tank definitions, and automation rules that will be applied to individual Flight Log Books created for specific aircraft. Purpose: Flight Log Book Setup serves as the master configuration that: Defines which aircraft models and configurations use specific flight log book types Establishes meter reading requirements and forecast amounts Configures fuel tank definitions and capacities Sets up engine tracking parameters Controls discrepancy and work order automation Determines post-flight inspection requirements Manages replenishment tracking Key Concepts: Concept Description Flight Log Book Type A unique identifier for a specific flight log book configuration template Applies To Defines which aircraft models and configurations use this setup Revision Control Tracks changes to flight log book configurations over time Associated Flight Log Books Individual flight log books created from this setup for specific aircraft Flight Log Book Setup is a template-based system. Changes to the FLB Setup affect new Flight Log Books created from the template. If the the FLB Setup is revised, modified and the new revision made active, then any existing Flight Log Books created from it will need to have the new revision applied manually. This is performed using an action "Change Flight Log Book Type" within the Flight Log Book application. The action can be called from the List tab to allow multiple Flight Log Books to be updated in one action. Application Access: Application Name: Flight Log Book Setup Application Code: PLUSAFLBSETUP Navigation: Go To → Flight Operations → Flight Log Book Setup

The Configuration section defines the core operational parameters for Flight Log Books created from this setup. Applies To​ The Applies To section determines which aircraft models and configurations will use this Flight Log Book Setup. Fields: Field Description Required Model Aircraft model (e.g., X-JET, A320, B737) Yes Configuration Specific aircraft configuration variant No Configuration Logic: When a new Flight Log Book is created for an aircraft: System checks the aircraft's model If a configuration is specified, system checks for exact match If configuration is blank, setup applies to all configurations of that model Most specific match (model + configuration) takes precedence Example Scenarios: FLB Setup Model Setup Configuration Aircraft Model Aircraft Config Match? Enable this feature for all operational aircraft to ensure consistent inspection practices and regulatory compliance. Discrepancy Options​ The Discrepancy Options section controls automation of work order creation and management of discrepancies reported during flight operations. Configuration Options: Option Description Impact Automatically Create Discrepancy Work Orders? Creates WO immediately when discrepancy is logged Ensures all discrepancies are tracked in work management Allow Discrepancy Resolution Before WO Completion? Permits closing discrepancy before associated work order is completed Provides flexibility for operational deferrals Allow Non-Grounding Discrepancies? Discrepancies marked as requiring independent inspection (RII) are not automatically closed. Automatically Cancel Discrepancy on WO Cancellation? Specify As of Date For: Determines which time is used as the official "Reading Date" for meter readings created through the Flight Data record: Option Description Use Case Arrival Time Uses the flight arrival time as the official date/time Most common - meters read at end of flight Departure Time Uses the flight departure time as the official date/time Special cases where departure time is critical Most operators use Arrival Time as the "as of" date because meter readings (flight hours, cycles) are typically recorded at the end of the flight. The Flight Log Book application is a comprehensive tool for managing and recording all aspects of aircraft flight operations in Maximo for Aviation. This application serves as the central hub for documenting flight activities, tracking aircraft status, managing crew assignments, and recording maintenance-related information discovered during flight operations. The Flight Log Book provides aviation maintenance and operations personnel with a complete view of: Flight data including crew assignments, fuel replenishments, and munitions usage Scheduled and completed flights Real-time aircraft status and meter readings Inspection schedules and maintenance requirements Discrepancies identified during flight operations Deferred maintenance items Equipment inspection lists and history The Flight Log Book integrates with other Maximo for Aviation applications to provide a seamless workflow from flight planning through maintenance execution. Key Features: Comprehensive flight data recording and management Real-time aircraft status monitoring Integration with preventive maintenance scheduling Discrepancy reporting and tracking Deferral management capabilities Equipment inspection tracking

The Flight Data section captures all essential information related to individual flights, including crew assignments, fuel and oil replenishments, and munitions usage. This section provides a complete record of each flight operation and serves as the foundation for operational reporting and analysis. Flight data is typically entered either: Manually by operations or maintenance personnel after flight completion Automatically through integration with flight data systems Via mobile applications used by flight crew Accurate flight data entry is critical for maintaining compliance with regulatory requirements and ensuring proper aircraft maintenance scheduling. Flight Data Fields: Field Name Description Required Flight Number Unique identifier for the flight Yes Aircraft Aircraft registration or tail number Yes Departure Date/Time Scheduled or actual departure time Yes Arrival Date/Time Scheduled or actual arrival time Yes Departure Location Origin airport or location code Yes Arrival Location Destination airport or location code Yes Flight Hours Total flight time in hours Yes Cycles Number of flight cycles (takeoff/landing) Yes Mission Type Type of mission or flight operation No Flight Crew​ The Flight Crew section allows you to assign and document all crew members associated with a specific flight. This includes pilots, co-pilots, flight engineers, and any other crew positions required for the mission. Crew Assignment Process: Navigate to the Flight Crew tab within the Flight Data section Click Add Row to add a new crew member Select the crew member from the person lookup Assign the appropriate crew position (e.g., Pilot, Co-Pilot, Flight Engineer) Enter flight hours for the crew member (if different from total flight time) Save the crew assignment Crew Position Types: Pilot in Command (PIC) - Primary pilot responsible for the flight Co-Pilot - Second pilot assisting with flight operations Flight Engineer - Crew member responsible for aircraft systems monitoring Navigator - Crew member responsible for navigation duties Loadmaster - Crew member responsible for cargo and weight distribution Additional Crew - Other crew positions as required by mission type Crew assignments are used for tracking individual flight hours, currency requirements, and qualification maintenance. Best Practices: Verify crew qualifications before assigning to flights Ensure crew duty time limitations are not exceeded Document any crew changes or substitutions Maintain accurate flight hour records for each crew member Replenishments​ The Replenishments section tracks all fuel, oil, and other consumable items added to the aircraft before, during, or after flight operations. This information is critical for: Fuel consumption analysis Cost tracking and allocation Maintenance planning (oil consumption trends) Operational efficiency monitoring Recording Replenishments: Navigate to the Replenishments tab Click Add Row to create a new replenishment record Select the replenishment type (Fuel, Oil, Hydraulic Fluid, etc.) Enter the quantity added Specify the unit of measure (gallons, liters, quarts, etc.) Record the location where replenishment occurred Enter the date and time of replenishment Save the record Common Replenishment Types: Type Description Typical Units Fuel Aviation fuel (Jet A, JP-8, etc.) Gallons, Liters, Pounds Engine Oil Lubricating oil for engines Quarts, Liters Hydraulic Fluid Hydraulic system fluid Quarts, Liters Oxygen Breathing oxygen for crew Pounds, Liters Coolant Engine cooling fluid Quarts, Liters Tracking oil consumption trends can help identify potential engine issues before they become critical failures. Fuel Consumption Analysis: Compare fuel loaded vs. fuel remaining to calculate consumption Track consumption rates per flight hour Identify anomalies that may indicate fuel system issues Support mission planning with accurate fuel requirement estimates Munitions​ The Munitions section documents all weapons, ordnance, and related equipment loaded, expended, or removed during flight operations. This section is primarily used for military aviation operations and provides critical tracking for: Weapons inventory management Mission effectiveness reporting Safety and compliance documentation Maintenance requirements triggered by weapons usage Munitions Tracking: Navigate to the Munitions tab Click Add Row to add a munitions record Select the munitions type from the catalog Enter the quantity loaded Record the quantity expended during the flight Document the quantity returned/remaining Specify the station or hardpoint location Add any relevant notes or comments Save the record Munitions Data Fields: Field Description Purpose Munitions Type Specific weapon or ordnance designation Inventory tracking Serial Number Unique identifier for serialized items Traceability Quantity Loaded Number of items loaded before flight Inventory management Quantity Expended Number of items used during flight Mission reporting Quantity Returned Number of items remaining after flight Inventory reconciliation Station/Hardpoint Aircraft mounting location Configuration tracking Lot Number Manufacturing lot identifier Quality control Munitions usage may trigger specific maintenance inspections or requirements. Ensure all expended munitions are properly documented. Maintenance Implications: Certain weapons may require post-firing inspections High-G maneuvers during weapons employment may trigger structural inspections Gun firing may require barrel inspections after specific round counts Weapons bay door cycles may affect maintenance schedules

The Flight Schedule section provides visibility into planned and scheduled flights for aircraft in your fleet. This section helps operations and maintenance personnel coordinate activities, plan resources, and ensure aircraft availability for scheduled missions. Schedule Management Features: View upcoming flights by aircraft, date range, or mission type Identify scheduling conflicts or aircraft availability issues Coordinate maintenance activities around flight schedules Track schedule adherence and on-time performance Plan crew assignments and resource allocation The Flight Schedule integrates with the Flight Log Book to automatically create flight records when scheduled flights are completed. Schedule Views: Daily View - Shows all flights scheduled for a specific day Weekly View - Provides a week-at-a-glance schedule Aircraft View - Displays schedule for a specific aircraft Mission Type View - Groups flights by mission category Planned Flights​ The Planned Flights section displays detailed information about upcoming flights, including departure and arrival times, locations, crew assignments, and mission requirements. This information is used to: Ensure aircraft are properly configured for planned missions Verify crew availability and qualifications Coordinate maintenance activities to avoid schedule conflicts Plan fuel, munitions, and other resource requirements Viewing Planned Flights: Navigate to the Flight Schedule section Select the Planned Flights tab Use filters to narrow the display by: Date range Aircraft Mission type Status (Scheduled, Confirmed, Cancelled) Click on a flight to view detailed information Planned Flight Information: Information Category Details Included Flight Details Flight number, mission type, priority Schedule Departure/arrival dates and times Locations Origin and destination airports Aircraft Assigned aircraft and configuration Crew Assigned crew members and positions Resources Fuel requirements, munitions, equipment Status Current status and any restrictions Flight Status Indicators: Scheduled - Flight is planned but not yet confirmed Confirmed - Flight is confirmed and resources are allocated In Progress - Flight is currently underway Completed - Flight has been completed and logged Cancelled - Flight has been cancelled Delayed - Flight departure has been delayed Regularly reviewing planned flights helps identify potential conflicts between maintenance requirements and operational schedules. Coordination with Maintenance: Check aircraft status before confirming flights Identify maintenance windows between scheduled flights Coordinate urgent maintenance with operations to minimize schedule impact Update flight schedules when maintenance delays occur

The Aircraft Status section provides a comprehensive, real-time view of the aircraft's current condition, including meter readings, inspection schedules, engine data, and maintenance holds. This section is essential for: Determining aircraft readiness for flight operations Monitoring maintenance requirements and due dates Tracking component life limits and time-change items Identifying issues that may affect aircraft availability Status Overview Features: Current meter readings (flight hours, cycles, calendar time) Upcoming inspection requirements Engine and APU operating parameters Active maintenance holds and restrictions Component status and life remaining The Aircraft Status section is automatically updated when flight data is entered or maintenance activities are completed. Status Indicators: Green - Aircraft is fully mission capable Yellow - Aircraft has minor restrictions or upcoming maintenance Red - Aircraft is not mission capable or has critical issues Blue - Aircraft is in scheduled maintenance Flight Meter Data​ The Flight Meter Data section displays current readings for all meters associated with the aircraft. Meters track various usage parameters that drive maintenance requirements, including: Flight hours (total time the aircraft has been airborne) Flight cycles (number of takeoff/landing sequences) Calendar time (elapsed time since manufacture or overhaul) Engine hours (operating time for each engine) APU hours (auxiliary power unit operating time) Viewing Meter Data: Navigate to the Aircraft Status section Select the Flight Meter Data tab Review current meter readings and last update dates Compare current readings to maintenance thresholds Identify meters approaching maintenance limits Meter Information Display: Column Description Meter Name Description of the meter (e.g., Flight Hours, Cycles) Current Reading Most recent meter value Last Update Date and time of last meter reading Average Rate Average accumulation rate (per day, per flight, etc.) Next Inspection Next maintenance requirement based on this meter Remaining Time/cycles remaining until next maintenance Meter readings must be accurate and up-to-date to ensure maintenance is performed at the correct intervals. Verify meter readings after each flight. Meter Types: Continuous Meters - Accumulate continuously (e.g., flight hours) Gauge Meters - Show current state (e.g., fuel quantity) Characteristic Meters - Track specific conditions (e.g., temperature) Delta Meters - Calculate differences between readings Best Practices: Update meter readings immediately after each flight Verify meter accuracy by comparing with aircraft systems Investigate significant deviations from expected accumulation rates Ensure meter readings are synchronized across all systems Scheduled Inspection Information​ The Scheduled Inspection Information section displays all upcoming and overdue inspections for the aircraft. This includes: Preventive maintenance inspections Calendar-based inspections Usage-based inspections (hours, cycles) Regulatory compliance inspections Special inspections (corrosion, structural, etc.) Inspection Display: Navigate to the Scheduled Inspection Information tab View inspections sorted by due date or priority Click on an inspection to view detailed requirements Identify overdue or approaching inspections Coordinate with maintenance planning to schedule work Inspection Information: Field Description Inspection Type Category of inspection (Phase, Letter Check, etc.) Description Detailed description of inspection requirements Due Date Calendar date when inspection is due Due At Meter reading when inspection is due Remaining Time/cycles remaining until due Status Current status (Scheduled, Overdue, In Progress) Work Order Associated work order number (if generated) Inspection Status Codes: Scheduled - Inspection is planned but not yet due Due Soon - Inspection is approaching due date/reading Overdue - Inspection has passed due date/reading In Progress - Inspection work has started Completed - Inspection has been completed and signed off Operating an aircraft with overdue inspections may violate regulatory requirements and void insurance coverage. Address overdue inspections immediately. Planning Considerations: Schedule inspections during planned maintenance windows Consider inspection duration when planning aircraft availability Coordinate multiple inspections to minimize downtime Ensure required parts and tooling are available before starting Verify qualified personnel are available to perform inspections Engine Data​ The Engine Data section provides detailed information about each engine installed on the aircraft, including: Engine serial numbers and part numbers Total time since new (TSN) and time since overhaul (TSO) Cycles since new (CSN) and cycles since overhaul (CSO) Operating parameters and trends Maintenance history and upcoming requirements Performance monitoring data Engine Information Display: Navigate to the Engine Data tab Select an engine position (e.g., Engine #1, Engine #2) Review current status and operating parameters View maintenance history and upcoming requirements Access detailed component information Engine Data Fields: Category Information Included Identification Serial number, part number, position Time/Cycles TSN, TSO, CSN, CSO Status Operational status, restrictions Performance EGT, fuel flow, oil consumption trends Maintenance Last maintenance, next due, work orders Components Module status, life-limited parts Performance Monitoring: Track exhaust gas temperature (EGT) trends Monitor oil consumption rates Identify performance degradation Compare parameters across engines Detect anomalies that may indicate developing issues Regular monitoring of engine performance data can help identify issues early, potentially preventing costly in-flight shutdowns or unscheduled maintenance. Life-Limited Parts Tracking: Monitor time/cycles remaining on critical components Plan component replacements in advance Coordinate replacements with scheduled maintenance Maintain traceability for all life-limited parts Ensure compliance with manufacturer requirements APU History​ The APU (Auxiliary Power Unit) History section tracks the operating history and maintenance activities for the aircraft's auxiliary power unit. The APU is a critical component that provides: Electrical power when main engines are not running Pneumatic power for engine starting Air conditioning and pressurization on the ground Backup power for essential systems APU Information: Navigate to the APU History tab Review APU operating hours and cycles View maintenance history and upcoming requirements Monitor performance trends and parameters Access component-level information APU Data Tracking: Data Type Description Operating Hours Total hours APU has been running Cycles Number of start/stop cycles Maintenance History Previous maintenance actions Performance Data EGT, oil pressure, fuel flow Component Status Status of APU modules and parts Upcoming Maintenance Scheduled maintenance requirements APU Maintenance Considerations: APU maintenance intervals are typically based on operating hours Start cycles can significantly impact component life Monitor oil consumption trends for early problem detection Coordinate APU maintenance with aircraft maintenance schedules Ensure APU is operational before extended ground operations APU failures can significantly impact aircraft operations, especially in remote locations. Regular monitoring and preventive maintenance are essential. Common APU Issues: High EGT during start or operation Excessive oil consumption Difficulty starting or maintaining operation Abnormal vibration or noise Electrical or pneumatic system anomalies Hold Item List​ The Hold Item List displays all active maintenance holds, restrictions, and limitations currently applied to the aircraft. Holds prevent the aircraft from being released for flight until specific conditions are met or maintenance actions are completed. Types of Holds: Safety Holds - Critical safety issues that ground the aircraft Maintenance Holds - Scheduled or unscheduled maintenance in progress Inspection Holds - Required inspections not yet completed Configuration Holds - Aircraft configuration does not meet requirements Administrative Holds - Documentation or regulatory compliance issues Operational Holds - Operational restrictions or limitations Viewing Hold Items: Navigate to the Hold Item List tab Review all active holds for the aircraft Click on a hold to view detailed information Identify actions required to clear each hold Monitor hold status and clearance progress Hold Information Display: Field Description Hold Type Category of hold (Safety, Maintenance, etc.) Description Detailed description of the hold reason Applied Date When the hold was placed on the aircraft Applied By Person or system that applied the hold Work Order Associated work order (if applicable) Status Current status of hold clearance Clearance Requirements Actions needed to clear the hold Aircraft with active safety holds must not be released for flight under any circumstances until the hold is properly cleared by authorized personnel. Hold Management Process: Hold Application - Hold is placed on aircraft when issue is identified Work Assignment - Maintenance work order is created to address issue Work Completion - Required maintenance or inspection is completed Verification - Work is inspected and verified by qualified personnel Hold Clearance - Hold is removed and aircraft is released for flight Best Practices: Review hold items before every flight release Ensure all required documentation is complete before clearing holds Verify that corrective actions actually resolve the issue Maintain clear communication between operations and maintenance Document all hold clearances with appropriate signatures and dates

The Aircraft Inspection and Maintenance section provides tools for documenting and managing maintenance activities discovered during flight operations or routine inspections. This section is critical for: Recording discrepancies found during pre-flight, in-flight, or post-flight inspections Creating maintenance work orders to address identified issues Tracking the status of maintenance actions Ensuring all discrepancies are properly resolved before flight release Discrepancies entered in the Flight Log Book are automatically integrated with the Maximo work management system for tracking and resolution. Inspection Types: Pre-flight Inspection - Conducted before each flight Through-flight Inspection - Conducted between flights Post-flight Inspection - Conducted after flight completion Daily Inspection - Conducted once per day Special Inspection - Conducted for specific purposes Discrepancies​ The Discrepancies section allows flight crew, maintenance personnel, and inspectors to document any issues, defects, or abnormalities discovered during aircraft operations or inspections. Proper discrepancy reporting is essential for: Maintaining aircraft safety and airworthiness Ensuring regulatory compliance Tracking maintenance trends and recurring issues Providing accurate maintenance history Creating a Discrepancy: Navigate to the Discrepancies tab Click Add Row to create a new discrepancy Enter a clear, detailed description of the issue Select the affected system or component Specify the severity level (Critical, Major, Minor) Indicate when the issue was discovered Add any relevant photos or documentation Save the discrepancy Discrepancy Information: Field Description Required Discrepancy Number Unique identifier for tracking Auto-generated Description Detailed description of the issue Yes System/Component Affected aircraft system or component Yes Severity Impact level (Critical, Major, Minor) Yes Discovered By Person who identified the issue Yes Discovery Date When the issue was found Yes Flight Phase When discovered (Pre-flight, In-flight, Post-flight) No Status Current status (Open, In Progress, Closed) Auto-updated Severity Levels: Level Description Action Required Critical Safety of flight issue Aircraft grounded until resolved Major Significant impact on operations Repair before next flight Minor Limited impact on operations Repair within specified timeframe Cosmetic No operational impact Repair during scheduled maintenance Critical discrepancies must be addressed immediately and may require notification to regulatory authorities depending on the nature of the issue. Discrepancy Workflow: Reporting - Discrepancy is documented in the Flight Log Book Review - Maintenance control reviews and prioritizes the issue Work Order Creation - Work order is generated to address the discrepancy Maintenance Action - Technicians perform required repairs or inspections Verification - Work is inspected and verified for quality Closure - Discrepancy is closed and aircraft is released Best Practices for Discrepancy Reporting: Be specific and detailed in descriptions Include exact locations (e.g., "Left main landing gear, forward trunnion") Document what was observed, not assumptions about the cause Include relevant operating conditions when the issue occurred Attach photos or diagrams when helpful Reference applicable technical manuals or procedures Update status as work progresses Common Discrepancy Categories: Structural - Cracks, corrosion, damage to airframe Systems - Hydraulic, electrical, pneumatic system issues Powerplant - Engine or APU problems Avionics - Navigation, communication, or instrument issues Flight Controls - Issues with control surfaces or systems Landing Gear - Gear, brakes, tires, or related components Environmental - Pressurization, air conditioning, oxygen systems

The Deferred Maintenance section manages maintenance items that have been identified but are allowed to be deferred under specific conditions. Deferral programs allow aircraft to continue operations with certain non-critical items inoperative, provided specific safety and operational requirements are met. Deferral Programs: Minimum Equipment List (MEL) - Defines equipment that can be inoperative Configuration Deviation List (CDL) - Allows operation with missing components Master Minimum Equipment List (MMEL) - Regulatory basis for MEL Operational Limitations - Restrictions applied when items are deferred Deferred maintenance items must be tracked carefully to ensure they are resolved within required timeframes and that operational limitations are observed. Deferral Categories: Category A - Must be repaired within specified time (usually 24 hours) Category B - Must be repaired within 3 consecutive calendar days Category C - Must be repaired within 10 consecutive calendar days Category D - Must be repaired within 120 consecutive calendar days Deferrals​ The Deferrals section provides detailed tracking of all deferred maintenance items, including: Description of the inoperative item or system MEL or CDL reference Deferral category and expiration date Operational limitations or restrictions Placarding requirements Maintenance actions required for clearance Creating a Deferral: Navigate to the Deferrals tab Click Add Row to create a new deferral Select the MEL or CDL item from the reference list Enter the discrepancy or reason for deferral Specify the deferral category Calculate and enter the expiration date Document any operational limitations Specify required placarding Save the deferral Deferral Information: Field Description Required Deferral Number Unique tracking identifier Auto-generated MEL/CDL Reference Reference to MEL or CDL item Yes Description Description of inoperative item Yes Category Deferral category (A, B, C, D) Yes Applied Date When deferral was applied Yes Expiration Date When deferral expires Yes Operational Limitations Any restrictions on operations If applicable Placarding Required placards or markings If applicable Status Current status (Active, Expired, Cleared) Auto-updated Deferral Management Process: Identification - Inoperative item is identified during operations or maintenance MEL Review - Maintenance control reviews MEL to determine if deferral is allowed Deferral Application - Deferral is documented with appropriate category and limitations Placarding - Required placards are installed on the aircraft Operations Notification - Flight crew is briefed on limitations Monitoring - Deferral expiration is tracked Resolution - Maintenance is performed before expiration Clearance - Deferral is cleared and placards are removed Operating an aircraft beyond a deferral expiration date is a serious violation of regulations and may result in enforcement action. Operational Limitations Examples: Maximum altitude restrictions Speed limitations Weather minimums (VFR only, day only, etc.) Passenger capacity restrictions Route or area restrictions Equipment requirements (e.g., must have specific backup systems) Best Practices: Review all active deferrals before each flight Ensure flight crew is aware of all limitations Monitor deferral expiration dates closely Plan maintenance to clear deferrals before expiration Verify placards are properly installed and visible Document all deferral-related communications Consider cumulative effects of multiple deferrals Deferral Clearance: Perform required maintenance to restore item to service Conduct operational checks to verify proper function Remove all placards related to the deferral Update deferral status to "Cleared" Document clearance with appropriate signatures Notify operations that limitation is removed

This topic provides a more detailed explanation of how Models, Variants and Revisions relate to configuration-managed assets. Every configuration managed asset, within Maximo, is evaluated (by the BDI and the system as a whole) in the context of it's current configuration attributes. The Models 'Core Concepts' and the Models(CM) application topics have described the concepts of Model, Variants and Revisions and provided an initial view on how these relate to CM assets. Model, Variant and Revision are the primary attributes that determine the Current Configuration of any configuration-managed asset. Here we go into more detail on how these primary configuration context attributes are determined for individual Asset records within Maximo. End Item assets End Item assets have these attributes explicitly recorded against them (using fields on the ASSET record, detailed in section Core Concepts - Assets). Non-End Item assets Non end item assets assume or inherit their current configuration based on a pre-determined priority order. That is to say, non-end item ASSET records do not explicitly reference a specific Model, Variant or Revision. This priority order, which determines a non-end item assets current configuration, is as follows: 1. End Item If the sub assembly asset has an ancestor which is an end item asset (asset above it in the asset hierarchy) that its current configuration is assumed/inherited from the first end item asset above it in the hierarchy. 2. Previous End Item If the sub assembly has been removed, from a parent end item asset, its current configuration is assumed based on where it was last installed. 3. New Asset Assemblies Record If the sub assembly has never been installed, as part of a parent end item assembly, its current configuration is taken from the New Asset Assemblies record it was created from. Initial Configuration If neither of the 3 situations above are applicable then the system may chose any Model, which references the Assets CM Item, as the context under which to validate the assets. This may be acceptable if the CM Item is only referenced in a single Model. If not then it is possible to apply an "Initial Configuration" explicitly to the non-end item asset. An Initial Configuration can be applied to a non-end item asset using the "Apply Configuration" action button located on the "Alternative Configuration" tab within the BDI Status dialog (found in the Assets (CM) application). This configuration will then be active against the asset until such time that the asset is installed into a higher end-item assembly. At this point this Initial Configuration is removed from the asset and point 1 above applies. BDI Status dialog showing how an Initial Configuration can be applied:

documents.t: The Build Hierarchy and Position Rules tab is used to define the physical structure of the Model and the configuration rules which form part of the allowed configuration. It allows the definition and visualisation of the parent/child relationship between the Build Positions.
The image below shows an example Build Hierarchy, formed from the Models Build Items, for a Rapid Transit Metro Train:

New positions can be added to the Model by right clicking a node and selecting the option "New Child" or "New Sibling". The dialog which is opened allows the user to specify the attributes for the new position: Detailed Field Information​ Field Name Description Example Value Indicator The type of position. A more detailed description of the indicator values are detailed below S Build Item Each Build Position is constructed from a Build Item representing the sub assembly/component that must be tracked, managed and maintained BEARING ASSY Position A Position value which when combined with the Build Item and Label can be used by the user to easily identify the build position LEFT Indenture The level of indenture within the Build Hierarchy that the position resides (read only and system generated based on where the position is added) 2 LCN A Logistic Control Number (LCN) that is used by the system to uniquely identify a build position within the current Model. The LCN value is also used to determine the parent/child relationship between positions in the Build Hierarchy L0001

Positions can be freely added, moved (using the Move Up/Down and Push/Up down) or deleted from the Build Hierarchy in the situation where NO Assets have been created from the Model. Once Assets are created from the Model then restrictions are imposed in terms of the movement of Build Positions. This is enforced as the LCN value of a position is used, as part of the Assets as maintained configuration history, to record which assets have been installed into a position over the assets lifecycle. If assets have been created then it is possible to add new positions (with new, unique, unused LCN values) and also delete build positions.

Positions can be deleted by the use of the trash can icon at the end of the build position node. In the case where a build position is deleted after assets have been created from the Model a record is created to record that the associated LCN value has been previously used for this Model. When new Build Positions are added these previously used LCN values are by default "skipped" when generating the LCN value for the new position. Previously used LCN values can be viewed and managed using the action "View Used Build Position LCNs". Records can be deleted from the "used" list if there is a specific requirement to re-use them.
The Build Hierarchy and Position Rules tab is also used to define configuration rules related to a Build Positions within the Model.

The information displayed in the "Position" sub tab relates to the selected build position within the build hierarchy. It is used to define rules and behaviour for the selected position eg. Whether a position is mandatory for a Variant, or whether a position applies to a Variant of the Model. Position Information​ The Position Information section gives general information about the Model. The fields within this section of the tab would not normally need to be modified. Position Quantities​ A standard position within a Model is referred to as a sub assembly position (Indicator=S). A standard sub assembly position provides the ability to install a child asset into the position within the associated asset hierarchy. In addition to this standard behaviour it is possible to also mark the sub assembly position as associated with a quantity. There are two distinct ways of defining this which have different behaviour when managing the assets associated with the position: Non-serialized If a position is flagged as a "Non-Serialized" position it is used to manage a quantity of non-serialized components. The Min and Max qty are validated by the BDI and if the quantity recorded against the position is outside of these limits a BDI problem code is raised against the asset position. The asset which is installed into the position can be considered as a "virtual" asset in that its only use is to be abe to record a quantity against it.
