One of the main elements of a Model are its "Configurations". The primary configuration type for every model is referred to as a "Variant". When a Model is created a default "Base Variant" is created automatically. Additional variants may be added as children of the based variant. A Variant is a way to define and manage structured deviations from a base Model. The Variants can be used to specify differences in configuration that are known, planned, and allowed. Variants allow organizations to model different configurations of the same asset type without duplicating the entire Model, which keeps the model definitions reusable, clean, and scalable. The Variants are used as part of the defintion of specific types of "Configuration Rules" configured within the Model. For example specific Positions or CM Items within the Model can be marked as not applicable to a particluar Variant. In the screenshot shown below we see a 4 and 6 car variant of the Model: Rapid Transit Metro Train (RTMT). The specific positions within the train are marked as applicable (and mandatory) in relation to each of the 4 and 6 car variants (how this is done is described in the following sections). In order to create an Asset, from a specific Model and Variant, the Variant must be set to be non-abstract (Abstract checkbox=N), and its status must be ACTIVE. A description and comment can also be given to each Variant. To add a new Variant to the Model the user can right click an existing Variant and in the context menu displayed, chose the option "Add Child" (Highlighted in the screenshot above). This will open a dialog where details of the new Variant can be entered and confirmed.

The Revisions table allows for the definition of one or more revisions. A "BASE REVISION" is created automatically for each new Model. Explanation of Revisions​ The main impact of a Model Revision is its relationship to Congfiguration Rules. When a Configuration Rule is defined, it is done so in relation to a specific revision of the Model. A configuration rule will only be applied to an Asset if the Revision applied to the Asset is equal to or greater than the revision defined on the configuration rule record. For example if there are two Revisions defined for the Model: Revision 0 (BASE REVISION) and Revision 1 (FIRST REVISION) If a configuration rule is created with the "Revision Context" = 1 then this will only apply to Assets which also have Revision 1 or greater applied to them. Assets created from the Model which remain at Revision 0 will not be subject to the rule. Note that a later revision of the same rule can be created to override prior revisions of the same rule type for a specific build position. If the "Auto Upgrade?" checkbox is set to Y, for a Revision, then the BDI will automatically upgrade the associated assets to the latest revision which is set to auto-upgrade.

The BDI Map Codes (sometimes referred to as Problem Codes) contains a list of every code which can be returned by the BDI to indicate a problem with the configuration of an Asset. A Map Code is a 3 letter code which indicates the type of problem together with a Description indicating under which conditions the code will be raised. Each code can be either active or inactive. If the code is marked as inactive, the BDI will skip executing the logic required to determine if the problem exists when validating the asset. In addition a Severity can be set for each Problem code. This will override the default Severity for that particular code. The default severity of each code is detailed in the BDI topic: Status and Problem Codes. Configuring Map Code Values​ The Map Code itself can be changed to a different 3 letter code if desired. Note that this change only effects the Model it is made against. To do this the following steps should be performed: In the Domains application, open the domain with name: PLUSABDICOND Add a new Synoym to the domain with the three letter code that should be used in replacement of the default code. The Internal Value sould be set to the original code. For example if the EBD code (Overdue Maintenance Event/PM) should be replaced with the code: PMD The Description is only used in the dispay of the Map Codes in the Models application: In the Models application delete the original code from the BDI Map Codes and save. Add a new row to the BDI Map Codes table and specify the replacement code, ensure the Active checkbox is set to true, and save again. The new replacement Map Code will then be active against the Assets where this Model is applied:

A model defines the engineering reference data and the allowable configuration for a type of complex asset. It's used: To defined the allowable configuration for a type of complex asset and possibly variants of that asset type. As a template from which to build asset hierarchies used to maintain assets of the type described by the Model. By the BDI to validate the as maintained configuration of the asset against its allowable configuration described by the Model (and highlights problems).
The Models main page contains general information about the Model and fields which control it's definition.

General fields​ Field Name Description Example Value Model The name of the Model with associated Description RTMT Item Set The Item Set to which the Model belongs. Models and CM Items are Item Set level objects due to their relationship with inventory SET1 Series The Series to which the Model belong. Models can optionally linked to a Series if there are a number of Models belonging to the Series. A SERIES Class The Class of Model eg LOCOMOTIVE. For information only and has no impact on system functionality. LOCOMOTIVE Code A Code for the Model type eg. ROLLING STOCK. USed to indicate general asset type. For information only and has no impact on system functionality. ROLLING STOCK Label System Used to indicate the system of labels used to identify a build position. For example, ATA, UIN or WUC. RAIL Predicted Life If set to true the system will attempt to calculate the current life of an asset based on past utiliziation. This is useful in very specific circumstances. Recommendation is to set to false (the default). N MSG-3? MSG-3 is a standard used in commerical aviation maintenance. When set to true additional fields related to this standard become available as part of a build position definition N Registration Required? When set to true the user will be forced to enter a Registration value for the top level asset when creating an asset from this Model in the New Asset Assemblies (CM) application Y Configuration Control fields​ Field Name Description Example Value LCN Structure Used to determine the format of LCN values used in the build hierarchy definition. LCN values are a unique value for each position in the build hierarchy and are also used to determine the parent/child relationship between build positions 1 (defaults to 1444444) Top LCN The character(s) used for the top LCN value in the Models build hierarchy. L Installable Indicates whether the Model is installable or not. Installable Models can be referenced by Build Positions marked as installation points in a parent Model. Sub Models are most often used when a complex sub assembly is used in multiple positions within a model or within multiple models. For example an engine. Y or N Provisional Serial Number The value is used by the BDI validation which determines if multiple assets share the same CM Item and Serial number. If the serial number of the asset is the same as the provisional serial number value it will not be considered as part of the logic which determines assets with duplicate CM Items/Serial Numbers TBC, TBD, UNKNOWN etc Validate Technical Records? Used to control whether the BDI will interpret, validate and take action on Technical Records related to the Model and assets created from the Model. Y or N Security Restriction? Used to control who can access the Model and Assets created from it. If set to Y the Model must be added to the users Security Group in order for them to continue to be able to access it. N MEL? Indicates if the Model defines a Mininum Equipment List. a MEL can be used to determine if the Asset is in valid configuration based on a minimum number of required items that must be installed and operational (servicable) N

The Build Items are a list of the main components (typically tracked and serialized) that are then used to create a build hierarchy representing the physical structure of the complex asset. They are related to one or more labels (typically one) and one or more CM Items which represent parts which provide the same fit, form and function of the component. Each Build Item records name must be unique within the Model it is contained within. When defining the Build Items and Build Hierarchy of a Model it is recommended that it is defined to the level at which it needs to be tracked and maintained in practice. Over-engineering an ACM model definition can lead to performance issues, user frustration, and increased maintenance overhead. The goal should be to model only what needs to be controlled or validated, and no more. Always try to balance precision with usability. Build Item fields​ Field Name Description Example Value Build Item The name of the Build Item. Must be unique within the Model it is contained within. STARTER GENERATOR Category The category of the Build Item for example HARDWARE or SOFTWARE. Value is optional HARDWARE Icon An image file name. The image will be displayed in the Build and Asset Hierarchy for each node created from the Build Item. The image file names must be incorporated into the maximo.ear file by way of a customization archive. starter-generator.gif. Label fields​ Labels are used (together with build item name and position value) to allow a user to easily identify a position within a complex asset hierarchy. Field Name Description Example Value Label Systen The name of the Build Item. Must be unique within the Model it is contained within. RAIL Label The label used as part of the build hierarchy definition. If a Build Item has multiple labels then a unique Default for Position value should be specific for each. This is so the system can identify which label to use for each build postion created from the build item. 10-00 Default for Pos A position value associated with the label. Used to determine which label to display for a build position LEFT CM Item Fields​ Field Name Description Example Value CM Item The CM Item related to the selected Build Item. Multiple CM Items, which provide the same fit, form and function, can be related to each Build Item. By default these are two-way interchangeable with each other Default? One CM Item related to a Build Item can be marked as the default. When creating an asset hierarchy from the Model, within the New Asset Assemblies (CM) application, the default CM Item will be chosen for a sub assmebly asset. This is unless it has been marked as not-applicable to the Variant of the Model being created. Y or N

The New Aircraft and Equipment application enables users to create configuration-managed (CM) asset hierarchies from Model definitions. This application streamlines the process of creating complex asset structures by leveraging the engineering data defined in the Model application, ensuring consistency and accuracy in asset creation. Asset Assembly Types: The New Aircraft and Equipment application supports two primary types of asset assembly creation: Complete Asset Assembly - An entire assembly starting with an end-item as the top-level asset within the assembly Examples: Complete aircraft, engine or other complex equipment which exists as a Model. Creates the full hierarchy from top-level asset down to all sub-components Ideal for new aircraft deliveries Partial Asset Assembly - A sub-assembly where the top-level asset corresponds to a position in the Model's build hierarchy at a level of indenture greater than 1 Examples: Landing gear assembly, APU etc Creates only a portion of the complete asset hierarchy Useful for creating spare rotable assemblies or replacement components The New Aircraft and Equipment application uses the Model as a template to generate asset data, ensuring that created assets conform to the as-designed configuration and include all required components, meters, and relationships. Key Capabilities: Generate complete or partial asset hierarchies from Model definitions Automatically create sub-assembly records based on build hierarchy Configure asset numbering schemes with prefixes and suffixes Define serial number patterns for components Convert existing non-CM assets to CM-managed assets Support bulk data loading via Maximo Integration Framework (MIF) Validate rotating items before asset creation Create assets in inventory locations (storerooms) Support background processing for large asset hierarchies Integration Points: Model Application - Source of build hierarchy and configuration rules Part Number Master - Defines Part Numbers and their attributes Master Task Cards - Linked to Part Numbers for PM generation Aicraft and Equipment Applications - Used to manage and view as-maintained Aicraft and Equipment. BDI (Build Data Interpreter) - Validates created Aicraft and Equipment assemblies

The New Aircraft and Equipment application allows for a structured process that guides users through the process of defining, configuring, and creating asset hierarchies. Step-by-Step Workflow​ 1. Create a New Record Begin by creating a new New Aircraft and Equipment record: Navigate to the New Aircraft and Equipment application Click New Aircraft or Equipment or use the + button Enter a New Asset value that will be used as the Asset number of the top-level asset Alternatively, configure the field (PLUSANEWASSET.ASSETNUM) to use the standard Asset autokey (see configuration section below) 2. Specify the Part Number Enter or select the Part Number corresponding to the top-level asset of the new assembly 3. Select Model and Configuration Choose the specific configuration: Use the lookup on either the Model or Configuration field The lookup presents all applicable values for the selected Part Number including: Model Variant Position (if creating a partial assembly) If creating a partial asset assembly where the Part Number is used in multiple positions, select the record with the specific position corresponding to the assembly you wish to create Selecting the correct Model, Variant, and Position combination is critical as it determines the entire build hierarchy that will be generated. Verify your selection before proceeding. 4. Enter Required Information Complete the essential asset details: Field Description Required Example Serial Manufacturer serial number Yes XF8181 Registration Aircraft registration or tail number Depends on "Registration Requied?" checkbox in the associated Model IBMXF-1 Asset Status Initial status of the asset Yes OPERATING 5. Specify Location Define where the asset will be located: Enter a Location for the asset If an Inventory Location (storeroom) is specified, the asset will be added into the storeroom on creation This is useful for creating spare rotable assemblies that will be held in inventory For operational aircraft, specify the operating location (e.g., airport, maintenance base) 6. Define Date Information Set critical dates for the asset: Date Field Description Importance Receipt Date Date asset was received Transactions cannot be performed before this date Date of Manufacture Date asset was manufactured Earliest allowable transaction date if before Receipt Date First Flight Date Date of first flight (aircraft only) Used for warranty and aging calculations Date of Transfer of Title Ownership transfer date Legal and financial tracking Date of Entry into Service Date asset entered operational service Warranty and maintenance program start date Transactions such as installation and removal of child assets cannot be performed with an "As of Date" that is before the Receipt Date or Date of Manufacture (whichever is the earliest date). Plan these dates carefully. 7. Configure Sub Assembly Prefixes Define how child asset numbers will be generated: Enter Equipment Prefix - Text to prepend to child asset numbers Enter Equipment Suffix - Starting number for sequential numbering The Asset Prefix and Suffix values are concatenated to form the asset number of each sub-assembly asset Example: Equipment Prefix: XF001- Equipment Suffix: 001 Generated child asset numbers: XF001-001, XF001-002, XF001-003, etc. This approach is particularly useful when creating demo or test asset assemblies where systematic numbering is desired. Child asset numbers (PLUSANEWSUB.ASSETNUM) can also be configured to use the standard Asset autokey instead of the prefix/suffix approach. See the configuration section for details. 8. Configure Serial Number Generation Define how child serial numbers will be generated: Enter Serial Prefix - Text to prepend to child serial numbers Enter Serial Suffix - Starting number for sequential numbering The same concatenation logic is used to generate serial numbers for child assets as for asset numbers Example: Serial Prefix: XF Serial Suffix: 8182 Generated child serial numbers: XF8182, XF8183, XF8184, etc. 9. Add Meters Define meters to track asset usage and life: Navigate to the Meters tab Click Add Row to manually add meters Alternatively, use the Create Meters from CM Build action to automatically add meters Create Meters from CM Build Action: Analyzes all Master Task Cards linked to the specified Part Number Identifies meters used in the Meter Frequency of these related Master Task Cards Automatically adds these meters to the Meters table of the New Aircraft and Equipment record Ensures consistency between maintenance requirements and meter tracking Meter Configuration: Field Description Example Meter Meter code FC (Flight Cycles), FH (Flight Hours) Description Meter description Flight Cycles, Flight Hours Initial Reading Event Event that establishes initial reading Date of Manufacture, Date of Installation Initial Reading Date Date of initial reading 01/01/2023 Initial Count Starting meter value 350.00 (FC), 1,000.00 (FH) Default? Whether this is the default meter Checked by default for the Primary Meter By default, meters added to the New Aircraft and Equipment record are automatically added to all child assets within the assembly, ensuring consistent meter tracking across the entire asset hierarchy. Meters can also be automatically added to the asset records generated by assigning a Meter Group to the individual Part Number Master records. It is not possible to specify initial counts when using this mechanism so it may be necessary to update these to actual values after the asset assembly is created. 10. Generate Sub Assemblies Create the sub-assembly structure: Click the Create Sub Assemblies from CM Build action The system generates sub-assembly information based on: Selected Part Number Selected Model Selected Variant Selected Position (if applicable) Related Model data and build hierarchy This action creates records in the Sub Assembly Details table representing each component in the build hierarchy. 11. Review Sub Assembly Details Verify the generated sub-assembly information: Navigate to the Sub Assembly Details tab Review each sub-assembly record for accuracy Verify the following information: Column Description Verify Label Build hierarchy label Matches Model definition Position Position code in build hierarchy Correct position assignment Build Item CM Item part number Correct part number Parent Parent asset number Correct parent-child relationship Aircraft or Equipment Generated asset number Follows numbering scheme Part Number Component part number Matches build hierarchy Monitoring Type Condition monitoring type Appropriate for component Serial Generated or assigned serial number Unique and follows pattern Category Asset category Correct classification The Part Numbers and Serial Numbers of the generated sub-assemblies can also be updated using the Maximo Integration Framework. This is recommended to avoid manually entering large amounts of data (which is prone to error). Sub Assembly Details Tabs: The Sub Assembly Details section includes multiple tabs for additional configuration: Initial Readings - Configure initial meter readings for each sub-assembly Consumable Parts - Define consumable parts associated with sub-assemblies Condition Monitoring - Set up condition monitoring points Warranty - Configure warranty information for components 12. Activate the Record Prepare for asset creation: Review all information for accuracy and completeness Change the status of the New Aircraft and Equipment record to ACTIVE This status change indicates that the data has been verified and is ready for asset creation Only ACTIVE records can be used to create assets Once the status is changed to ACTIVE and assets are created, modifications to the record become restricted. Ensure all data is correct before activation. 13. Create Aircraft and Equipment Execute the asset creation process: Click the Create Aicraft or Equipment action to initiate creation of the asset hierarchy Choose whether to run the process in the foreground or background: Foreground - Process runs immediately, user waits for completion Background - Process runs asynchronously, user receives email notification on completion Background Processing: Recommended for large asset hierarchies (e.g., complete aircraft with thousands of components) Prevents timeout issues for long-running processes Allows user to continue working while assets are created Email notification includes success/failure status and any error messages Pre-Creation Validation: Before asset creation begins, the system performs validation: Verifies that all Rotating Items linked to the asset or its children are valid within the target Organization Checks for duplicate asset numbers Validates that all required fields are populated Confirms that Part Numbers exist and are active within the target Organization Ensures parent-child relationships are valid Asset Creation Process: Creates the top-level asset record Creates all child asset records in hierarchical order Establishes parent-child relationships Adds meters to all assets Sets initial meter readings Creates asset specifications Links to rotating items (if applicable) Triggers BDI validation (if configured) Generates Task Card records (via BDI)

The New Aircraft and Equipment application includes options to automatically add related data to created assets, streamlining the asset creation process and ensuring completeness. Available Options: Option Description When to Use Consumable Parts? Automatically add consumable parts to assets When assets require specific consumables for maintenance Measure Points? Automatically add condition monitoring measurement points For assets with condition monitoring programs Warranty Contracts? Automatically add warranty contract information For new assets under manufacturer warranty Configuration: Check the appropriate boxes in the "Automatically Add" section Configure the specific items to add in the respective tabs: Consumable Parts tab - Define consumable parts and quantities Condition Monitoring tab - Define measurement points and parameters Warranty tab - Define warranty contracts and coverage Benefits: Ensures consistency across all created assets Reduces manual data entry after asset creation Maintains compliance with maintenance programs Supports warranty tracking from asset creation

For organizations that prefer to use Maximo's standard autokey functionality for asset numbering rather than manual entry or prefix/suffix patterns, the New Aircraft and Equipment application can be configured to automatically generate asset numbers. Configuration Requirements: To enable autokey generation for asset numbers, direct database updates must be performed. This configuration should be done during initial system setup or during a planned maintenance window. SQL Configuration Script: -- Configure autokey for top-level assets (PLUSANEWASSET) UPDATE maxattribute SET autokeyname='ASSETNUM', canautonum=1, defaultvalue='&AUTOKEY&' WHERE objectname='PLUSANEWASSET' AND attributename='ASSETNUM'; UPDATE maxattributecfg SET autokeyname='ASSETNUM', canautonum=1, defaultvalue='&AUTOKEY&' WHERE objectname='PLUSANEWASSET' AND attributename='ASSETNUM'; -- Configure autokey for sub-assembly assets (PLUSANEWSUB) UPDATE maxattribute SET autokeyname='ASSETNUM', canautonum=1, defaultvalue='&AUTOKEY&' WHERE objectname='PLUSANEWSUB' AND attributename='ASSETNUM'; UPDATE maxattributecfg SET autokeyname='ASSETNUM', canautonum=1, defaultvalue='&AUTOKEY&' WHERE objectname='PLUSANEWSUB' AND attributename='ASSETNUM';

documents.t: The New Aircraft and Equipment application provides powerful functionality to convert existing non-configuration-managed assets into CM-managed assets. This capability is essential during system implementation when migrating legacy asset data or when adopting configuration management for existing assets. Conversion Overview: The conversion process updates existing non-CM asset records with the information necessary for the system to treat them as CM-managed assets, including: Setting the CM Part Number on the ASSET record and creating additional CM related data. Establishing Model and Variant associations Defining parent-child relationships based on build hierarchy Adding required meters Conversion Workflow: 1. Prepare the Record Create a new New Aircraft and Equipment record as described in the standard workflow Critical Step: Populate the Existing Asset field with the existing non-CM managed asset number This field tells the system to update an existing asset rather than create a new one 2. Configure Top-Level Asset Specify the CM Item, Model, and Variant for the existing asset Enter the serial number and other identifying information Ensure the configuration matches the actual physical asset 3. Generate Sub Assemblies Use the Create Sub Assemblies from CM Build action The system generates the expected sub-assembly structure based on the Model 4. Map Existing Assets to Positions This is the critical step that maps existing assets to their positions in the build hierarchy: Review each generated sub-assembly record Update the Aircraft or Equipment field on each sub-assembly record to specify the existing non-CM managed asset number that corresponds to that position This mapping tells the system which existing asset should be placed in each position Example Mapping: Position Build Item Generated Asset Existing Asset to Map 1 ENGINE-LEFT RTMT001-001 ENG-12345 (existing) 2 ENGINE-RIGHT RTMT001-002 ENG-67890 (existing) 14LAVD AVIONICS-POD RTMT001-003 AVI-11111 (existing) 5. Execute Conversion Use the Create Asset action The system presents a dialog listing each existing asset record The dialog asks the user to confirm the update to these existing asset records Review the list carefully to ensure correct assets are being converted Confirm to proceed with the conversion Conversion Process Details: When the conversion is executed, the system performs the following updates to each existing asset: Asset Record Updates: Field Update Action CM Item Set to the part number from the build hierarchy Model Set to the selected Model Variant Set to the selected Variant Parent Updated to match the build hierarchy (if asset has no parent) Position Set based on position in build hierarchy Configuration-Managed Flag Set to true Build Hierarchy Attributes Populated from Model definition Meter Management: Meters defined in the New Aircraft and Equipment record are added to existing assets if they don't already exist Existing meters are preserved and not duplicated Initial readings are set for newly added meters Existing meter readings are retained Parent-Child Relationships: If the asset does not have a parent, its parent is updated to correspond to its position within the build hierarchy of the Model Existing parent-child relationships are preserved if they match the build hierarchy Conflicts between existing relationships and build hierarchy are flagged for review Conversion Validation: Before and during conversion, the system validates: Existing assets exist and are accessible No duplicate asset numbers in the mapping CM Items are valid and configuration-managed Model and Variant are properly defined Parent-child relationships are valid Meters are properly configured The conversion process makes permanent changes to existing asset records. Always test the conversion process in a non-production environment first and ensure you have a database backup before proceeding. Best Practices for Conversion: Data Preparation Audit existing assets before conversion Document current asset hierarchy Identify any data quality issues Clean up asset data before conversion Mapping Strategy Create a mapping document showing existing assets to positions Verify serial numbers match physical assets Confirm parent-child relationships Review with operations and maintenance teams Phased Approach Convert assets in phases (e.g., by aircraft, by system) Start with a pilot conversion of one asset Validate results before proceeding with bulk conversion Monitor BDI validation and PM generation after conversion Testing Test conversion in development environment first Verify all asset attributes are correctly updated Confirm meters are properly added Test PM generation after conversion Validate reporting and queries work with converted assets Communication Notify users before conversion Explain changes to asset records Provide training on CM-managed asset features Document the conversion process and results Post-Conversion Activities: After conversion, perform these activities: Run BDI validation on converted assets Verify Task Card generation is working correctly Review asset hierarchy in Aicraft or Equipment application Validate meter readings and history Test work order creation and completion Update documentation and training materials Monitor for any issues or anomalies

documents.t: The New Aircraft and Equipment application supports bulk data creation and updates through the Maximo Integration Framework (MIF), enabling efficient processing of large volumes of asset data. MIF Integration Benefits: Bulk creation of New Aircraft and Equipment records Mass update of serial numbers, CM Items, and meter information Automated data loading from external systems Integration with legacy system migrations Support for data validation before asset creation MXLoader Support: An example MXLoader file is provided in the Loading Data topic that demonstrates: Creating New Aircraft and Equipment records via MIF Updating sub-assembly information Setting meter configurations Preparing data for asset creation Typical MIF Use Cases: Initial System Load Load fleet data during implementation Create New Aircraft and Equipment records for all aircraft Populate sub-assembly information Set initial meter readings Bulk Updates Update serial numbers for multiple assets Change CM Items across multiple records Modify meter configurations Update date information Integration with External Systems Import data from ERP systems Sync with manufacturer databases Load data from spreadsheets Integrate with procurement systems Using MIF for bulk data loading is particularly useful when creating multiple similar assets (e.g., a fleet of identical aircraft) or when migrating data from legacy systems.

The New Aircraft and Equipment application provides tabs for configuring additional asset-related information that will be automatically added to created assets. Consumable Parts​ Define consumable parts that are associated with the asset: Navigate to the Consumable Parts tab Add consumable items that are regularly used with the asset Specify quantities and units of measure These parts will be automatically linked to created Aircraft and Equipment records Use Cases: Lubricants and fluids specific to the asset Filters and consumables for maintenance Standard hardware and fasteners Cleaning and preservation materials Condition Monitoring​ Configure condition monitoring measurement points: Navigate to the Condition Monitoring tab Define measurement points for the asset Specify monitoring parameters and thresholds Set up monitoring schedules Monitoring Types: Vibration analysis points Temperature monitoring locations Pressure measurement points Oil analysis sampling points Performance parameter monitoring Warranty​ Set up warranty information for new assets: Navigate to the Warranty tab Define warranty contracts Specify coverage periods and terms Link to warranty providers Set up warranty tracking parameters Warranty Information: Warranty start and end dates Coverage scope and limitations Warranty provider contact information Claim procedures and requirements Parts and labor coverage details Configuring these additional elements ensures that created assets have complete information for maintenance planning, condition monitoring, and warranty management from day one.

documents.t: The Part Number Master application is a foundational component of Maximo for Aviation that provides comprehensive management of part numbers, including Configuration-Managed (CM) part numbers. This application serves as the central repository for all part number definitions that are essential for aircraft configuration management, maintenance planning, and inventory control. The application is a modified version of the core Manage Item Master application with additional fields, tabs and related attributes to manage configuration-managed part numbers. Configuration-Managed Part Numbers represent the components that make up an aircraft or complex asset. CM Part Numbers are used in Models and form part of the engineering reference data used to define an as-designed configuration. They establish the baseline for what components should be installed on an aircraft and provide the framework for tracking actual vs. designed configurations. The Part Number Master is tightly integrated with the Model application, Master Task Cards, Operators Maintenance Program (OMP) and the Build Data Interpreter (BDI) to ensure configuration compliance and automated maintenance program management. Key Capabilities: Define and manage part numbers with comprehensive attributes Establish configuration-managed part numbers for aircraft components Define serial number formats and ranges for traceability Create serial range usable-on codes (UOCs) for effectivity management Display Master Task Cards for CM Parts (used for automated Task Card generation) Support interchangeable parts and alternates Manage part specifications, vendors, and storeroom locations Track part assembly structures and relationships Define ATA chapter codes for system organization Support both hardware and software part number management

The Part Number Master application contains numerous fields that define the characteristics, attributes, and relationships of each part number. Understanding these fields is essential for consultants implementing the system and ensuring data quality. Core Identification Fields​ Field Name Description Example Value Required Part Number The unique identifier of the Part APU-7766 Yes Part Set The Part Set to which the Part Belongs AVINPNSET Yes Description A detailed description of the part Auxillary Power Unit Yes The Part Number in combination with the Part Set field forms its unique identifier in the system and once saved, it cannot be changed. Plan your part numbering scheme carefully before implementation. Classification and Categorization​ Field Name Description Example Value Notes Category The type of part (HARDWARE, SOFTWARE, etc.) HARDWARE Used to classify parts by type Software Type The type of software if categorized as SOFTWARE FLS (Field Loadable Software) Only applicable for software parts ATA Code Air Transport Association chapter code 49-00 (APU) Organizes parts by aircraft system Commodity Group High-level commodity classification AVIONICS For procurement and inventory grouping Commodity Code Detailed commodity classification NAVIGATION_EQUIPMENT More specific than commodity group Common Part Categories: HARDWARE - Physical components and assemblies SOFTWARE - Software loads, firmware, and applications ENGINE - Aicraft Engine APU - Auxilliary Power Unit Configuration Management Fields​ Field Name Description Example Value Impact Configuration-Managed? Indicates if this is a CM part number ☑ (checked) Enables use in Models and BDI validation Aircraft Part? Indicates if this part is used on aircraft ☑ (checked) Determines if part appears in aircraft BOMs Rotable? Indicates if part is repairable/rotable ☑ (checked) Affects inventory and maintenance processes Serial Format Format of serial numbers for this part AANNN Defines expected serial number pattern Position Code Required? Whether position code is mandatory ☐ (unchecked) Controls position tracking requirements Hazardous? Indicates if part contains hazardous materials ☐ (unchecked) Triggers special handling requirements Configuration-Managed parts are the foundation of the Model application. Only CM parts can be used to define aircraft build hierarchies and configuration rules. Serial Format Patterns: A - Alphabetic character N - Numeric digit X - Alphanumeric character (letter or number) AANNN - Two letters followed by three numbers (e.g., AB123) NNNNN - Five numeric digits (e.g., 12345) AANNNN - Two letters followed by four numbers (e.g., XY1234) Inventory and Procurement Fields​ Field Name Description Example Value Purpose Shelf Life? Indicates if part has a shelf life ☐ (unchecked) Triggers expiration tracking Preferred? Indicates if this is a preferred part ☐ (unchecked) Guides procurement decisions Kit? Indicates if part is a kit of components ☐ (unchecked) Affects issue and inventory processes Replenishment? Indicates if part should be auto-replenished ☐ (unchecked) Triggers automatic reorder Add as Consumable Part? Add to consumable parts list ☐ (unchecked) Makes part available for consumption Monitoring and Tracking​ Field Name Description Example Value Usage Monitoring Type Type of condition monitoring applied HT (Hard Time) Defines monitoring approach Meter Group Group of meters associated with part ENGINE_METERS Links to meter definitions Meter Specific meter for tracking usage FLIGHT_HOURS Primary usage meter MSDS Material Safety Data Sheet reference MSDS-12345 Safety information reference Monitoring Type Examples: CM - Condition Monitoring HT - Hard Time LLP - Life Limited Part OC - On Condition ST - Soft Time

The Serial Ranges functionality allows for the definition of one or more Serial Range Usable on Codes (UOC) for each configuration-managed part number. Serial Range UOCs are a powerful feature that enables precise control over which serial numbers of a part are applicable to specific aircraft or configurations. Purpose of Serial Range UOCs: Define effectivity for specific serial number ranges Support engineering changes that affect only certain serial numbers Enable configuration rules based on component serial numbers Track which part serial numbers are valid for specific aircraft The Serial Range UOC is a unique value within the context of the CM Part Number that is used to identify a range of serial numbers. These UOCs are then referenced within specific configuration rules in the Model application to specify which positions or part numbers are valid for specific ranges of end item serial numbers. Serial Range UOC Structure​ Each Serial Range UOC consists of two key components: Component Description Example Serial Range Usable on Code Unique identifier for the serial range UOC1, UOC2, EARLY_BUILD, LATE_BUILD Serial Range Expression Defines the actual serial numbers included 10001..19999, 20000..99999 Serial Range Expression Formats: The Serial Range Expression can be defined using three different formats: Comma-Separated List of Serial Numbers Format: Individual serial numbers separated by commas Example: AA001, AA004, AA009 Use Case: When only specific, non-consecutive serial numbers are affected Result: Only the explicitly listed serial numbers are included Range Notation Using Double Dots Format: Start serial number, double dots (..), end serial number Example: A001..A100 Use Case: When a continuous range of serial numbers is affected Result: Includes A001, A002, A003, ... all the way to A100 inclusive Note: The system automatically includes all serial numbers between start and end Combination of Both Formats Format: Mix of individual serial numbers and ranges Example: A001, A003, A006..A009 Use Case: When you need both specific serial numbers and ranges Result: Includes A001, A003, A006, A007, A008, A009 Note: Provides maximum flexibility for complex effectivity scenarios Serial Range Expression Examples: Scenario UOC Code Serial Range Expression Interpretation Early production units EARLY_PROD 10001..19999 All serial numbers from 10001 through 19999 Late production units LATE_PROD 20000..99999 All serial numbers from 20000 through 99999 Specific test units TEST_UNITS T001, T002, T005, T010 Only these four test serial numbers Mixed effectivity MIXED_EFF 1001..1050, 1075, 1100..1150 Range 1001-1050, plus 1075, plus range 1100-1150 Pre-modification PRE_MOD 5001..5500, 5550..5600 Two separate ranges before modification Post-modification POST_MOD 5601..9999 All units after modification cutoff Creating Serial Range UOCs​ Step-by-Step Process: Navigate to the Serial Ranges tab in the Part Number Master Click Add Row to create a new serial range UOC Enter a unique Serial Range Usable on Code (e.g., UOC1, EARLY_BUILD) Define the Serial Range Expression using one of the three formats Validate the expression syntax Save the serial range UOC Serial Range UOC codes must be unique within the context of a single part number. However, the same UOC code can be used across different part numbers with different serial range expressions.

The Master Task Cards for Part Number section displays all Master Task Cards that are related to the current configuration-managed part number. This relationship is fundamental to Maximo for Aviation's automated preventive maintenance generation capability and ensures that the correct maintenance tasks are created for each installed component. Relationship Overview: Master Task Cards are linked to part numbers in the Master Task Card application The relationship is typically established when creating or editing Master Task Cards Multiple Master Task Cards can be associated with a single part number Each task card defines specific maintenance requirements for the component The relationship drives automated PM generation through BDI validation Master Task Card Information Display​ The Master Task Cards table shows key information about each related task card: Column Description Example Value Master Task Card Unique identifier for the task card 1013, 1014, 1015, 1016 Task Code Short code identifying the task type RS, DS, GVI, DVI ATA Code ATA chapter code for the task 49-00 (APU) Master Task Card Type Category of maintenance task COMPONENT, AIRCRAFT, SYSTEM Description Brief description of the task APU Overhaul, APU Life Limit, APU Inspection OMP Operators Maintenance Program reference XJET-001

The Master Task Cards application is a foundational component of Maximo for Aviation that enables the creation and management of master maintenance task definitions. Master Task Cards serve as templates that define maintenance requirements, frequencies, and procedures for configuration-managed (CM) components and aircraft systems. Purpose and Function: Master Task Cards act as the authoritative source for maintenance task definitions that are: Linked to one or more configuration-managed (CM) Part Numbers Used to automatically generate Task Cards for applicable assets (Aircraft or Equipment) Integrated with Operators Maintenance Programs (OMPs) Maintained with full revision control and change tracking Organized by ATA chapters and maintenance phases Master Task Cards are the bridge between manufacturer maintenance requirements (imported via MTL) and operational maintenance execution (Task Cards on assets). They ensure consistency and compliance across the fleet. Key Capabilities: Define maintenance tasks with comprehensive frequency criteria Link tasks to configuration-managed part numbers Support multiple frequency types (calendar, meter-based, iterations) Configure task actions that affect related tasks Manage task revisions with full change tracking Generate Task Cards automatically for applicable assets Support check-based maintenance organization Enable task extensions and deferrals Integrate with OMP and BDI for automated Task Card generation Integration Points: Part Number Master - Links tasks to CM part numbers MTL Application - Source for manufacturer task requirements OMP Application - Organizes tasks into maintenance programs Aicraft and Equipment Application - Displays generated active Task Cards on the Maintenance Plan tab BDI (Build Data Interpreter) - Automates Task Card generation Work Orders - Execution of maintenance tasks Job Cards - Detailed work instructions and resource requirements

Understanding the structure and fields of a Master Task Card is essential for consultants implementing the system. Header Information​ Core Identification Fields: Field Description Example Required Task Number Unique identifier for the Master Task Card XJET-APU-OVH Yes Description Descriptive name of the task APU Overhaul Yes Status Current status of the Master Task Card ACTIVE, DRAFT, PNDREV, INACTIVE Yes Revision Revision number for change tracking 0, 1, 2 Yes Operator Operating organization IBM Yes ATA Code ATA chapter code 49-00 (APU) Yes Master Task Card Type Category of task COMPONENT, AIRFRAME, CHECK, EVENT Yes Task Code Short code for task type RS, OPC, DET, GVI Yes Master Task Card Type Values: The Master Task Card Type field categorizes tasks by their nature and purpose: Type Description Usage AIRFRAME Airframe Task Tasks performed on the aircraft structure, systems, or zones. Not specific to a removable component. Examples: fuselage inspections, wing structural checks, system functional tests. CHECK Maintenance Check Used to group tasks with similar frequencies into larger maintenance events (A-Check, C-Check, etc.). Checks organize multiple tasks for efficient planning and execution. COMPONENT Component Task Tasks performed on specific removable components or assemblies. Linked to part numbers and follow the component through its lifecycle (on-wing, in-shop, in-storage). Examples: engine overhaul, landing gear inspection, APU service. EVENT Event-Based Task Maintenance tasks triggered by specific events rather than time or usage intervals. Examples: post-lightning strike inspection, after hard landing check, following bird strike. Selecting the correct Master Task Card Type is critical as it determines how the task behaves, how Task Cards are generated, and how the task integrates with asset configuration management. Task Code Examples: Code Description Typical Usage RS Restoration Overhaul, major repair, rebuild OPC Operational Check Functional verification, system operation test DET Detailed Inspection Thorough visual inspection with specific criteria GVI General Visual Inspection Basic visual check for obvious defects DIS Discard Time-change item, life-limited part replacement SVC Service Lubrication, replenishment, routine servicing FNC Functional Check System functional test, operational verification Special Instructions​ The Special Instructions section contains flags that are used for information purposes only. They highlight specific requirements or nature of the task to be performed. Field Description Impact ALI? Airworthiness Limitation Item.
